key_insight: Parallel Trajectory Tempering keeps Energy-Based Model training near equilibrium, making maximum-likelihood learning stable and practical on multimodal, data-scarce scientific datasets.
engineering_relevance: This provides a drop-in training alternative with Persistent Contrastive Divergence-like cost but better sampling quality, likelihood estimation, and robustness for scientific generative modeling.
method: Track the optimization path with parallel trajectories to preserve equilibrium sampling during training.
Use reservoir sampling and adaptive optimization to improve efficiency and stability.
Estimate thermalization time, equilibrium samples, and log-likelihood with little extra cost.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Restricted Boltzmann Machines and discrete tabular data show consistently better performance than existing EBM training methods and stronger results than state-of-the-art deep generative models.
watch_item: PTT depends on maintaining effective mixing and a reliable reservoir across training, so implementation quality and hyperparameter tuning may strongly affect performance.
paper_title: Equilibrium Training of Energy-Based Models with Parallel Trajectory Tempering
